response.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT AVG(modelconf) AS baseline FROM compliancecase), grp AS (SELECT brokrepstat AS status, AVG(modelconf) AS avg_conf FROM compliancecase GROUP BY brokrepstat), qual AS (SELECT g.status, g.avg_conf, b.baseline FROM grp g CROSS JOIN base b WHERE g.avg_conf > b.baseline), ref AS (SELECT AVG(avg_conf) AS qual_mean FROM qual) SELECT q.status, q.avg_conf AS avg_modelconf, q.avg_conf - q.baseline AS diff_from_baseline, q.avg_conf / r.qual_mean AS ratio_to_qual_mean FROM qual q CROSS JOIN ref r WHERE q.baseline IS NOT NULL AND r.qual_mean IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: The baseline is AVG(modelconf) over all rows of compliancecase, so rows with NULL modelconf are excluded, consistent with 'averages ignore missing values'.
Cases with no status are those where brokrepstat IS NULL; GROUP BY places them in one group with a NULL status value. Empty strings are not treated as missing.
'Mean of the qualifying statuses' averages' is an unweighted AVG over the per-status averages of the statuses above the baseline, not over individual cases.

The ratio divides by the qualifying mean without a zero guard. If that mean is 0 the query raises a division-by-zero error in PostgreSQL-style engines; the request does not say what to return in that case.
